reaction.episode: CORRECTION through Nov 11 close, data fresh: SPX 7,619.38 is 2.87% off its 120-day high, 0.69% below its 50-day and 3.89% above its 200-day; SMH $506.96 is 24.5% off its high and BETWEEN_ZONES, $1.96 above Zone 2; NVDA $173.73 is BELOW_ZONE_2 after closing $1.27 under the $175 floor; VIX 17.49 has rolled over from a 5-day high of 28.18; HY OAS 3.3 is calm; mechanical tally 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: The Watch stance is wrong if SMH prints Zone 2 and holds it with the tally reaching 3 of 4 while NVDA reclaims $175 — that is a live bottoming process, not a correction to watch — or if SPX closes below its 200-day with HY OAS above 4%, which voids the ladder entirely and re-grades the episode as a regime break.

ladder.response: Re-arm Tranche A: 25% deployment on the zone print per the deployment ladder, sized to the confirmed print, not the intraday dip
ladder.trigger: SMH closes inside Zone 2 ($470–505) with VIX below 25 and mechanical tally at 3 of 4 or better

ladder.response: Treat as the failed first bounce — no chasing, no new probes; wait for the second low to form and hold before any deployment
ladder.trigger: SMH or SPX bounces into the failure zone (SMH $580–600 / SPX $7,750–7,820) and fails to hold a close above it

ladder.response: Stand down: no new probes, Tranche A re-arm is void, and the correction is re-graded as a regime break
ladder.trigger: HY OAS breaks above 4% or VIX closes above 25, or SPX closes below its 200-day average ($7,334.28)

ladder.response: Tranche C conditions met: 50% deployment on the confirmed bottom, per the ladder
ladder.trigger: Confirmed bottom: failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds, with the 10-year yield falling — or a held close above SPX $7,750–7,820 / SMH $580–600

ladder.response: Zone occupancy flips to confirmed — the Nov 9 bottom void is repaired and the probe case is live again on the re-earned print
ladder.trigger: NVDA closes back above $175 while SMH is inside Zone 2

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail setup is the live risk: SMH bounced 4.82% on Nov 11 and NVDA 2.87%, but both remain deep off their highs with NVDA below its zone floor — a first bounce after a 28.6% NVDA drawdown and a VIX spike to 28.18 is exactly where bull traps form. Entries wait for the zone print plus tally at 3 or better; no chasing the bounce, and any rally into the SMH $580–600 / SPX $7,750–7,820 failure zone is judged on whether it holds a close above it, not on the size of the up day.

strategyPosture: Watch. The tape is a CORRECTION with a 2-of-4 mechanical tally: VIX has rolled over and credit is calm, but zone occupancy has not printed and the Nov 9 bottom call is void — NVDA closed below its $175 Zone 2 floor. Nothing is armed until a fresh Zone 2 print arrives with the tally at 3 or better.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and concentrated in the names that dominate the index by weight — NVDA alone is 32.4% off its high — so index-level calm masks real damage underneath. But a rollover needs credit stress or a 200-day break, and neither is present. Position as rotation: leadership is changing, not collapsing.
themes.dataAnchor: The index is not confirming that story. SPY is only 2.9% off its 52-week high and -1.34% over one month, while the Mag 7 average sits 16.33% off their highs — a 13.43-point divergence gap. Credit is calm: HY OAS is 3.3% and bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold). SPX closed Nov 11 at 7,619.38, just 0.69% below its 50-day average and 3.89% above its 200-day.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover — Mag 7 Weakness Inside a Calm Index
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad market break: the Magnificent 7 are deep off their highs and the AI complex is down 25% in a month, so the index must be rolling over.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or SPX closing below its 200-day average ($7,334.28) would convert rotation into rollover.

themes.counterRead: The price says the AI cycle is over; the revenue lines say the cycle is still compounding and the market is repricing the multiple, not the demand. NVDA below its zone floor voids the Nov 9 bottom call — the zone print has to be re-earned on a close, not assumed from oversold readings. The split inside the complex (AVGO +5.7% vs NVDA -5.11% today) is the market sorting durable infrastructure from headline-exposed names.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA closed Nov 11 at $173.73, $1.27 below the $175 Zone 2 floor, and is 28.6% off its 120-day high with an RSI of 25.5 — deeply oversold. SMH is 24.5% off its high at $506.96, sitting $1.96 above the top of Zone 2 ($470–505). Against that price damage, NVDA revenue is still growing 61.4% year over year, and AVGO — the other AI-infrastructure bellwether — is up 5.7% today on revenue growing 55% year over year.
themes.label: AI Semis in the Drawdown — NVDA Below Its Zone Floor
themes.narrative: The AI trade is broken: NVDA is down 25.5% in a month, fell 5.11% today to $164.64, and the FBI investigation into Huang's alleged chip shipments has turned a valuation story into a headline-risk story.
themes.watchFor: NVDA reclaiming $175 on a close with SMH printing inside Zone 2 ($470–505) flips zone occupancy and re-arms the Tranche A probe.

themes.counterRead: The basket-wide selloff treats VST as a momentum proxy for the AI power narrative, but the fundamentals that matter — raised guidance, insider buying at the trough, 2.6x price-to-sales — point the other way. The gap between the basket's price action and VST's own numbers is the opportunity; the risk is that the power trade was always a derivative of the AI capex narrative, so a deeper AI repricing drags it regardless.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is the conviction promotion of this run (score 83): $135.11, -28.6% from its peak, revenue growing 19.1% year over year, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. Q3 printed Nov 6 with EPS $3.25 vs $2.98 consensus and 2026 guidance raised — the upside confirmation Jun set as the condition. VST is already a holding, and the next leg Jun named is the 50-day at $145.08, which has not printed yet.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI Power — VST at the Trough With Insiders Buying
themes.narrative: Power names rode the AI data-center story up and are now giving it back: VST is 28.6% off its peak and 10.95% lower over one month, and the whole nuclear basket (CCJ -11.35%, GEV -12.47%, OKLO -14.57%, SMR -13.46% over one month) is selling off with it.
themes.watchFor: VST closing above its 50-day average ($145.08) arms the next leg; a close below $130 with the nuclear basket still falling says the trough is not holding.

themes.counterRead: The market is pricing a software demand collapse that the revenue lines do not show: DDOG's revenue inflection is RECOVERY, not deterioration. The divergence is the setup — but NOW's own revenue inflection reads DETERIORATING, so the theme is not uniform and names have to be picked on their own numbers, not the sector's.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG is the top conviction name (score 82): revenue growing 27.7% year over year with an 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow (29.2% margin), while the stock sits 38.5% below its high with an RSI of 31.9. NOW is 42% off its high at $101.44 with an RSI of 30.3. The dislocation list is dominated by sentiment-driven declines — 13 of the 31 names are FULL_SIGNAL with SENTIMENT_DRIVEN as the decline reason — not by deteriorating revenue.
themes.label: Software / SaaS — Revenue Recovering While Prices Fall
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is the new crowded short: NOW is 42% off its high, DDOG 38.5%, and the sector reads as the next leg of the AI unwind as customers cut spend.
themes.watchFor: DDOG holding above $180 into its Jan 14 earnings window with no pre-announcement, or NOW's next print confirming the DETERIORATING inflection — either would settle whether this is repricing or real demand damage.

themes.counterRead: The narrative ran ahead of the fundamentals: treasury premiums and 2x leverage only work while Bitcoin rises, and with BTC down double digits the premium becomes a liability that compounds the fall. CONL at -45.25% in a month is leverage doing exactly what leverage does. Nothing in the input shows a fundamental turn — the washout is the price catching down to a narrative that had run too far, and holdings here are exposure to be sized, not averaged down into.
themes.dataAnchor: The unwind is broad and fast: over one month BTC-USD is -11.87%, COIN -23.36%, BMNR -15.51%, DOGE -16.15%, and CONL -45.25% (down 5.92% today). BMNR, DOGE, and CONL are all holdings. IBIT is -12.36% and ETH-USD -15.62% over the same month, so this is not a single-name problem — the whole crypto complex is de-rating together while the 10-year sits at 4.88% and real yields at 2.68%.
themes.label: Crypto / Leverage Washout — the Premium Is Unwinding
themes.narrative: Crypto treasury and leveraged products were the cycle's easy leverage: CONL, BMNR, and DOGE let holders ride Bitcoin with a premium attached, and the premium was the trade.
themes.watchFor: BTC-USD stabilizing above its one-month range with IBIT flows turning positive for a full week would mark the washout ending; another leg down in BTC with CONL falling faster than 2x says leverage is still unwinding.
